_role: Model defaults. One place. Env vars MODEL / ADAPTER override without editing.
name: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
_system_policy: null = no system turn (see src/common/chat.py). NEVER change this to the template default without recording it: an injected 'You are Qwen, a helpful assistant' contaminates every judgment.
_gen_note: Per-role generation profiles. src/judge/judge.py:hf_generator merges `gen` with `gen[role]`, role being 'answer' (cmd_pairs) or 'judge' (cmd_judge).

WHY THE CAPS ARE GENEROUS. max_new_tokens is a CEILING, not a target -- generation stops at EOS, so a cap costs wall-clock only on runs where it binds. In r0 answers ran ~550 tokens and judgments ~1100-2000, so neither cap is expected to bind. What a cap does NOT buy you is VRAM headroom: an earlier version of this note claimed VRAM was not a constraint, and then a 24 GB card OOMed. The KV cache is real (~56 KB/token, so 2 sequences of 12k tokens is ~1.4 GB) but it is not what fills the card -- the weights are. See _4bit_note. A cap exists to stop a repetition loop running forever, nothing else.

WHY THE ANSWER CAP IS ALSO GENEROUS. Capping answers low looks like a free speedup and is not: a truncated answer is not a concise answer, it is a broken one, and the judge would then score `completeness` against an artefact this harness created. Brevity is one of the things being measured, so it has to be the model's choice, never the harness's.

judge._note: The five-step protocol quotes both answers back before it reaches the verdict block. Judgments in the pilot were dying mid-STEP-3 and mid-STEP-4 at 900. `truncated` is now recorded per judgment, so if this still binds you will see it named as truncation rather than inferred from a parse failure.
judge._temperature_note: Cooler than the answer role. A judge sampling at 0.7 cannot be self-consistent or order-invariant, and those are two of the six validation gates. Still above 0 so k_samples measures something.

gen._cap_note: Generous on purpose. max_new_tokens is a CEILING and generation stops at EOS, so a cap only costs wall-clock on the runs where it binds. In r0 answers ran ~550 tokens and judgments ~1100-2000, so neither of these is expected to bind at all -- they exist only to stop a repetition loop running forever.

_device_map_note: Everything on GPU 0, deliberately NOT 'auto'. 'auto' does not fail when a model is slightly too large -- it strands modules on CPU and copies them back on every forward, which reads as a slow GPU and then OOMs mid-generation trying to land one. On a 24 GB card with bf16 weights it stranded the lm_head (152064 x 3584 x 2 B = 1.02 GiB), which was the exact failing allocation. An explicit single-device map leaves accelerate nowhere to offload to, so from_pretrained raises at load instead.
_4bit_note: VRAM arithmetic for Qwen2.5-7B on 24 GB: bf16 weights are 7.62e9 x 2 B = 15.2 GB, plus ~1.4 GB KV cache for 2 sequences of ~12k tokens, plus activations and allocator fragmentation -- it fits on paper and does not in practice. 4-bit NF4 weights are ~4.3 GB, which leaves the card with room to spare. Set false only on a 40 GB+ card, and check the pilot s/pair before assuming it is faster.
